description: Airbrush Surrealism is an illustration aesthetic that diffuses compressed-air, smooth painting methods with fantasy, kitschy, dream-like subjects prominent from the late 1960s to the mid-1980s, featuring neon glows, glossy chrome, and impossible floating objects, where its main focus of the aesthetic incorporates supersaturated colors, juxtaposed/floating chrome textures, objects, lightning, 'X-Ray' technical illustration, vibrant gradients, hot pinks, deep purples, electric blues, chrome spheres, liquid surfaces, metallic ribbons, disembodied geometric shapes, planets, shapes or crystal structures floating in gradients along with high-contrast laser beams, artificial sunbursts, and glowing horizons, along with this aesthetic's appearance influenced later retro internet art movements like vaporwave, which drew heavy inspiration from classic surrealism artists like Salvador Dalí.
